key_insight: PolyNets turn known physics into a training-free neural network: a continuous-time polynomial dynamics module plus a recurrent integrator that preserves the numerical scheme while running efficiently on hardware.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to emulate PDE solvers with GPU-friendly throughput and scalable ensembles without paying the cost of model training, while retaining solver-like accuracy.
method: Encode governing equations as polynomial dynamics in a continuous-time neural representation
Use a simple recurrent network to implement discrete-time integration
Exploit known coefficients so the tensor graph can run training-free and parallelized
evidence_signal: On the 1D KdV equation, PolyNet matched CPU/GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta accuracy across grid resolutions, 10^6 time steps, up to 10^4 trajectories, and different initial amplitudes.
watch_item: Performance depends on known governing coefficients and preserving the chosen numerical scheme, so applicability may be limited when the physics is incomplete or strongly uncertain.
paper_title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
